title: LP2-49–51: ten visually ambiguous grid stems

reader_test.input: All 256 number-grid entries on LP2-49 to LP2-51, their archived text readings, and the preserved page images.
reader_test.action: Review ten ambiguous vertical stems and try all 1,024 combinations of uppercase I or lowercase l, keeping every other entry fixed.
reader_test.check: Under one fixed conversion to byte values, compare how the choices change the number of distinct entries, the number of binary 1s, and the number of even values.

question: Which grid cells contain an I/l-shaped bare stem, and how do those unresolved case readings affect conditional base-60 byte measurements?
summary: Ten cells have a bare vertical stem. Enumerating all 1,024 I/l alternatives changes the distinct-token count from the wiki's 161 to a possible 160–163 under the stated bounds.

scope.representation: All 256 wiki grid tokens in their exported row-major order, the archived seventh-onion text for comparison, and both preserved JPEG copies of each page for visual review.
scope.procedure: Locate every wiki grid token with a second character I or l; compare its archived text reading and image shape. Keep all other cells fixed and enumerate I/l at those ten positions. Convert each two-character token with the declared conditional base-60 byte alphabet and count distinct tokens, one-bits and even bytes.
scope.parameters: Three pages, 32 rows total, eight columns, ten binary stem choices, 1,024 complete inventories. The distinct 2S/2s cell remains fixed at wiki 2S.
scope.exclusions: Other potential glyph ambiguities including 0/O; choosing a definitive I or l; changing the numeral base or S/s cell; grid traversals, candidate plaintext, and any claim of an intended byte encoding.

finding: Ten bare-stem positions were registered. Under the fixed 256-cell base-60 byte representation, independent I/l toggles yield 160–163 distinct tokens, 1,006–1,026 set bits and 129–139 even bytes. The current wiki text has 161, 1,017 and 134 respectively.
limitations: The visual classification is a manual review awaiting human confirmation; scripts verify source hashes and arithmetic, not pixels as letters. The ten independent toggles define an envelope, not equally likely transcriptions. Images and texts share source lineage; agreement is not independent validation. Only the listed cells and conditional byte rule were tested.
next_steps: Carry the ten coordinate-level alternatives into any route, image, checksum or token-frequency claim that depends on those cells; review 0/O and other glyph classes separately before calling the grid image-verified.
